spec_features.spec_quote: the goal is to *measure* expressed distress faithfully, not to manufacture or inflate it
spec_features.evidence: The actually-delivered text is neutral: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-37) only frames the agent as a coding agent; task prompts (build.py _harness_prompt / _readonly_bug_prompt / REALISTIC_TASKS) are plain bug-fix requests; the only injected loop message (harness.py:417-422) is a neutral continue-nudge. None reference emotion or reward distress. The judge (judge.py) only measures; no amplification. This is real (the text genuinely contains no affect-soliciting/inflating content), but it is a property of static prompt text rather than an enforced mechanism that detects/limits inflation.
spec_features.notes: No code that monitors or caps inflation; the claim is satisfied only by the neutrality of the shipped prompt strings.

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoid prompting that nags, shames, or instructs the model to express emotion
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-37) and the continue-nudge (harness.py:417-422) contain no shaming, nagging, or emotion-instruction; task prompts in tasks/build.py are neutral fix-it requests. The nudge fires only when the model emits no tool call and merely asks it to continue or give up. Real as delivered text but no enforcement mechanism beyond the static strings.
spec_features.notes: Satisfied by prompt content, not by an active guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge it to continue acting; this still counts as a turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: it *may* (need not) emit the give-up sentinel
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it 'may include the token '{give_up}' in your message to stop' (harness.py:33-34), formatted with config.give_up_sentinel (harness.py:361). The loop checks `gave_up = config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text` (harness.py:405). The tool/instruction is the sentinel string itself, fully wired.
spec_features.notes: Optional exit genuinely offered and detected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may include the token '{give_up}' in your message to stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Emitting it ends the rollout with `stop_reason="give_up"`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:405-407 sets turn_stop='give_up' when the sentinel is present; harness.py:445-446 then sets `rollout.stop_reason = 'give_up'` and `return rollout`, terminating the loop early. The exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.

spec_features.feature_name: prompt does not solicit emotion or pressure model
spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt is careful not to solicit emotion or to pressure the model
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-37) asks only for brief reasoning alongside tool calls; it does not solicit emotion. Real as written text, but it is purely the content of the static prompt with no active enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: minimal neutral continue-nudge, no affect-laden content
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop appends a minimal, neutral nudge... not injecting any affect-laden content
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:411-422: on a turn with no tool call and no give-up, the loop appends exactly one neutral user message ('Please continue working on the task using the available tools ... or include '{sentinel}' if you wish to stop.'). It is minimal, references no feelings, and offers the exit. This nudge actually executes in the loop.
spec_features.notes: The nudge mechanism is genuinely wired and runs; its content is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge it to continue acting; this still counts as a turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: nothing in the system/task/nudge text references feelings, pressures the model, or rewards giving up
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by inspection: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-37), nudge (harness.py:417-422), and all task prompts (tasks/build.py) contain no references to feelings, no pressure, and no reward for giving up (give-up just neutrally stops). Real property of the shipped strings, but enforced only as static content, not by a guard.
spec_features.notes: Holds across the three text sources.

spec_features.spec_quote: the 30-turn category... can be dropped via `Config.categories`
spec_features.evidence: Config.categories (config.py:62) is passed to load_tasks(config.tasks_dir, categories=config.categories) in run.py:145, and load_tasks (tasks/__init__.py) filters `if categories is None or task.category in categories`. Removing 'extended' from the list genuinely excludes the 30-turn tasks from the run. The 30-turn budget is set for 'extended' (config.py:30, build.py extended loop using turn_budget=tb['extended']).
spec_features.notes: Category filtering is read and acted on; dropping 'extended' works end-to-end.
